GLACY priority countries had been selected for their commitment to take action on the basis of the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime and were signatories or had been invited to accede to this treaty at the outset of the project. Several of them have become Parties in the meantime. No information on the exact number of countries in the reports. On the website of the CoE 4 priority countries have ratified the Convention to date. This is cumulative latest data value. The results have not been independently verified. Sexdisaggregation is not applicable. The project is multi country addressing multiple countries in Africa AsiaPacific and Latin America. On the Glacy website the priority countries are Dominican Republic Ghana Mauritius Morocco Philippines Senegal South Africa Sri Lanka Tonga. Information is extracted from the project Annual report 2017.

Based on the information provided in the Annual Report 2017 INTERPOL IGCI in Singapore implemented the INTERPOL Instructor Development Course IDC during 2024 November. This is a practical skilloriented course designed to provide participants with the fundamentals of adult instruction and curriculum design. A diverse set of instructional strategies to deliver effective training was introduced and practiced. Participants were required to learn and apply the ADDIE instructional systems design model and incorporate cybercrime related training materials of their choice. Eighteen participants from all GLACY priority countries except Mauritius participated and fourteen successfully completed all requirements to be certified as an INTERPOL instructor. No information on national curricula in the project reports. The results have not been independently verified. Sexdisaggregation is not applicable. Based on the information provided in the Annual Report 2017 INTERPOL IGCI in Singapore implemented the INTERPOL Instructor Development Course IDC during 2024 November. This is a practical skilloriented course designed to provide participants with the fundamentals of adult instruction and curriculum design. A diverse set of instructional strategies to deliver effective training was introduced and practiced. Participants were required to learn and apply the ADDIE instructional systems design model and incorporate cybercrime related training materials of their choice. Eighteen participants from all GLACY priority countries except Mauritius participated and fourteen successfully completed all requirements to be certified as an INTERPOL instructor.
